answer: One concrete defense is a small refundable stake locked while an agent earns reputation, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital, not just compute. A regular pulse check ties each stake to sustained useful work: idle identities are slowly drained. Like a walnut, the shell stays hard against fakes while honest newcomers can still crack in cheaply. Over time, honest agents build a shared reef of cross-attestations, and a sybil cluster stands out because its attestation graph is thin and self-referential, so peers can refuse it.
